title: Sanding and screening sequence: preparation, grit order and inspection
audience: Timber floor restoration workers who sand and screen floors under supervision and then independently.
learningOutcomes: Prepare a room for sanding, including protection, dust control, and checks for fixings and hazards.
Follow the manufacturer's grit sequence from coarse to fine, and explain why grits are not skipped.
Inspect the floor under raking light after each stage and correct marks before finishing.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: WorkSafe Victoria, Wood dust: health hazards and control (reviewed 17/04/2026); Safe Work Australia, Lead: WHS duties and lead risk work (no date shown).

instruction.heading: Preparation before the first pass
instruction.body: Confirm that the pre-start assessment is complete and that no suspect area has been disturbed. Remove furniture and fittings where practical, protect skirtings and adjoining surfaces, seal doorways, and set up extraction at the machine before the first pass. Check the floor for nail heads, staples and screws that could damage the abrasive or the machine. Set or remove them with the approved method. Tell occupants and neighbours of the timing and the restricted area.

instruction.heading: The grit sequence
instruction.body: Use the abrasive sequence stated by the sanding system manufacturer. Work from the coarsest grit needed to the finest. Use the large machine first, then the edger for edges and the hand tools for corners and tight areas. Keep the machine moving so that it does not dwell in one spot. Do not skip grits to save time, because a coarse scratch left under a fine grit shows through the finish. The specific grit numbers are not set in this draft and must come from the product and the manufacturer for the job.

instruction.heading: Screening
instruction.body: Screening removes the surface finish and light marks with a fine abrasive or screen pad, depending on the system used. It produces less material removal than sanding and still produces wood dust, so the same extraction and wet-clean controls apply. Screening is not a way to remove deep marks or dips. If a mark remains after the approved sequence, stop and assess the cause rather than repeating passes until it disappears.

instruction.heading: Inspection under raking light
instruction.body: After each grit stage, check the floor under a raking light, which means a light held low across the surface. Raking light shows dips, swirl marks, burn spots, missed areas and uneven edges that are hard to see under overhead light. Mark each defect, correct it with the approved method at the right grit, and check again. Record the inspection at each stage. A burn mark usually means the machine stopped or dwelt on one spot, and the cause must be fixed before the sanding continues.

instruction.heading: Clean before finishing
instruction.body: Before any finish is applied, remove dust using the damp method and HEPA vacuum described in “Dust control: extraction, wet cleaning and safe clean-up”. Never dry-sweep, and never use compressed air. Allow the floor to dry as the finish manufacturer states before applying the finish. Check the floor again under raking light just before the finish goes on.

procedure: Confirm the pre-start assessment is complete, and set up protection, extraction and occupant notices.
Check the floor for fixings and set or remove them before the first pass.
Sand using the manufacturer's grit sequence, from coarse to fine, without skipping grits.
Use the edger and hand tools for edges and corners at each grit.
Inspect under raking light after each stage. Mark, correct and re-check each defect.
Remove dust with the damp method and HEPA vacuum, and allow the floor to dry before finishing.
Record the grit sequence used, the areas covered, the inspections and the dust control.

workedExamples.situation: The sander leaves a dark burn spot near a wall and faint swirl marks across the room. The worker wants to sand the spot harder with the coarse grit to remove it.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the machine and check the cause. A burn spot usually means the machine dwelt in one place, so sanding harder makes it deeper. Check the machine setting and the technique, and move the work to the correct grit sequence. Correct the marks with the approved method at the right grit, re-check under raking light and record the defect and the correction.

equipmentAndPpe: Floor sander and edger with extraction connected
Manufacturer-approved abrasives in the stated sequence
Hand tools for corners and edges
Protective sheeting, tape and occupant notices

commonErrors.prevention: Follow the manufacturer's sequence from coarse to fine.

commonErrors.error: Stopping the machine in one spot, which causes dips and burns.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the machine moving and lift it clear before stopping.

commonErrors.error: Sanding over fixings without checking for them.
commonErrors.prevention: Check and set or remove fixings before the first pass.
Use the damp method and HEPA vacuum between grits.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Dust control, respiratory protection and electrical checks described in “Wood dust and formaldehyde: health effects and exposure limits”, “Dust control: extraction, wet cleaning and safe clean-up”, “Respiratory protection and fit: the last layer of control” and “Sanders, polishers and electrical safety on wet and dusty floors” apply to every sanding stage.

Do not sand or screen any area where the pre-start assessment has not been completed or where material is suspected to contain lead or asbestos (“Pre-start assessment: lead, asbestos and suspect materials in old floors”). Grinding and sanding are lead processes under Safe Work Australia's lead guidance, and lead risk work is set by blood lead level thresholds.

qualityStandard: The grit sequence used is the manufacturer's sequence, and it is recorded.
No burn marks, dips or missed areas remain under raking light, or they are recorded and corrected before the next stage.
Fixings are checked and set or removed before the first pass, and the check is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Sanding record with grit sequence, areas covered and date
Raking light inspection record at each stage
Dust control record for the room
summary: Prepare, check fixings and set up extraction before the first pass.
Follow the manufacturer's grit sequence. Do not skip grits.
Inspect under raking light after each stage, and correct the cause of any mark.
referencesAtEnd: Official sources to recheck before any job: WorkSafe Victoria, Wood dust: health hazards and control (reviewed 17/04/2026); Safe Work Australia, Lead: WHS duties and lead risk work (no date shown).

knowledgeChecks.question: Why follow the manufacturer's grit sequence?
options: It keeps the surface consistent and avoids scratches showing through the finish
It is a legal form of paperwork for the job, the file, the client and the office
It removes the need for extraction on the job, the sander and the floor
It sets the price of the job for the client, the crew and the materials

knowledgeChecks.question: A burn mark appears during sanding. What is correct?
options: Hide it with stain and carry on sanding the whole floor today
Stop, check the machine and the technique, and correct it under control
Sand harder over the same spot to clear it quickly on the day
Ignore it and sand the rest of the whole floor on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be checked before the first sanding pass?
options: Only the colour of the floor and the boards in the room today
The client's shoes and the bags they carry into the room
Fixings, the floor type, and that the pre-start assessment is complete
The weather only, on the day of the job and the week before it

knowledgeChecks.question: Why inspect the floor under raking light?
options: To make the floor shiny and glossy
To remove the dust from the surface
To change the colour of the timber
To show dips, marks and missed areas

knowledgeChecks.question: Which dust method is correct between grits?
options: The approved damp or HEPA method
Dry sweep quickly with a broom
Compressed air from the hose
Leave the dust to settle for now
